html:
Judea was the hill country around Jerusalem in the southern Levant, and the name of the Jewish state there in Hellenistic and Roman times. On this map, in 1 BCE, it is the kingdom of Herod the Great, a client of Rome.

After the Maccabean revolt against the Seleucids, the Hasmonean dynasty ruled an independent Judea. In 63 BCE Pompey took Jerusalem and made it a Roman dependency. Rome named Herod king in 40 BCE, and he took power in 37 BCE. He rebuilt the Temple on a vast scale and built Caesarea and Masada, but was feared and hated.

Jesus was born near the end of his reign. When Herod died in 4 BCE, Augustus divided the kingdom among his sons, and in 6 CE made Judea a Roman province. Revolt broke out in 66 CE; Rome crushed it and destroyed the Temple in 70 CE. After the Bar Kokhba revolt, Rome renamed the province Syria Palaestina in about 135 CE.
